questions.prompt: Why do methods on Swift structures require the mutating keyword to modify stored properties, and what kind of variable do you need to call them? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that structures are value types whose properties cannot be modified by default
States that the mutating keyword explicitly allows modifying properties or reassigning self
Notes that mutating methods can only be called on var instances, not let constants

questions.modelAnswer: Structures in Swift are value types, so their instance methods cannot change stored properties by default. Adding the mutating keyword allows a method to change stored properties or assign a new instance to self. Because changing properties modifies the value, you can only call a mutating method on a var instance, never on a let constant.

questions.prompt: What is an automatic memberwise initializer in Swift? How can you add custom initializers to a struct without losing it? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Defines the memberwise initializer as an automatically created init for a struct's stored properties
Explains that writing a custom initializer inside the main struct body removes the memberwise init
States that putting custom initializers in an extension keeps the memberwise initializer

questions.modelAnswer: A memberwise initializer is an initializer Swift creates for a struct with labeled parameters for stored properties that need values. Properties with default values can be omitted, and a let constant with a value is left out. If you write a custom initializer inside the main struct body, Swift removes the automatic memberwise initializer. Put custom initializers in an extension to keep both.

questions.prompt: Explain failable initializers in Swift. What keyword declares them, and how do they signal failure? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that failable initializers are written with the init? keyword
States that they return an Optional instance of the type
Explains that writing return nil signals failure when setup cannot succeed

questions.modelAnswer: A failable initializer uses the init? keyword for cases where setup can fail on invalid inputs. It returns an optional instance of the type instead of a non-optional value. When setup fails, the initializer writes return nil so the caller gets nil and can unwrap the result safely.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an instance method and a type method in Swift? Which keywords declare type methods? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that instance methods are called on specific instances to use their own data
Explains that type methods are called directly on the type itself without an instance
States that type methods use static (or class in classes to allow overrides)

questions.modelAnswer: Instance methods are functions called on one specific instance, reading or changing that instance's own properties. Type methods are functions called directly on the type itself rather than an instance. Declare type methods with static func, or use class func in a class so subclasses can override them.

questions.prompt: Why do classes in Swift not require the mutating keyword on methods that modify variable stored properties? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that classes are reference types, so variables hold a reference to a shared instance
States that class methods modify the shared object's variable properties directly, even on let instances
Notes that mutating is only needed for value types like structs and enums

questions.modelAnswer: Classes are reference types, not value types. Calling a method on a class edits the shared instance directly through its reference, even when that reference is stored in a let constant. Because mutating only controls changes on value types like structs and enums, class methods can change var properties without writing mutating.
